[[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] (1999) * Second-team ''Parade'' All-American (1998) | bbr = boganke01 }} '''Keith Ramon Bogans''' (born May 12, 1980) is an American former [[basketball]] player who last served as an assistant coach for the [[New York Knicks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played college basketball for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. ==School and college career== Bogans attended [[The Langley School (Virginia)|The Langley School]] in [[McLean, Virginia]] and [[DeMatha Catholic High School]] in [[Hyattsville, Maryland]], and was an All-American first team honoree in his senior year. He was coached by [[Morgan Wootten]], leading DeMatha to a 34–1 record and a number three national ranking in 1999. He was recruited by the [[University of Kentucky]], and was a four-year starter for the Wildcats under coach [[Tubby Smith]]. In his senior year at UK, he led the 2002–03 Wildcats to a 16–0 sweep of the [[Southeastern Conference]] and the SEC Tournament title, finishing with an [[Elite Eight]] run in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]]. He was an All-American as a college senior when he averaged 15.7 points, 3.8 rebounds, 2.7 assists, and 1.2 steals. He was also 80-for-209 from three-point range. His illustrious collegiate career ended as he limped off the court at the [[Hubert H. Humphrey Metrodome]], after playing the game on a severely sprained ankle. The Wildcats ended up losing to [[Dwyane Wade]]'s Marquette squad in the Elite 8. On September 26, 2014, Bogans was inducted into the University of Kentucky Athletics Hall of Fame.[http://www.nationofblue.com/2014/09/congratulations-to-keith-bogans-wildcats-hall-of-fame Congratulations to Keith Bogans, Wildcats Hall of Fame!] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150224172125/http://www.nationofblue.com/2014/09/congratulations-to-keith-bogans-wildcats-hall-of-fame/ |date=February 24, 2015 }}{{Cite web |url=http://www.coachcal.com/30986/2014/09/bogans-inducted-uk-athletics-hall-fame-2/ |title=Bogans inducted into UK Athletics Hall of Fame |access-date=September 28, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141111223007/http://www.coachcal.com/30986/2014/09/bogans-inducted-uk-athletics-hall-fame-2/ |archive-date=November 11, 2014 |url-status=dead }} ==Professional career== ===Orlando Magic=== [[File:Keith Bogans.jpg|thumb|Bogans with the Magic, March 2008]] Bogans was chosen in the second round with the 43rd pick in the [[2003 NBA draft]] by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], but was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]] on draft day. Bogans started in half of the games he played in his rookie season, averaging 6.8 points, 4.3 rebounds and 2.9 assists per game. ===Charlotte Bobcats=== The Magic traded Bogans to the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] in exchange for [[Brandon Hunter]] on November 1, 2004. Bogans continued his development as a player for the Bobcats in the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]], starting in 42 of his 76 games and averaging 9.6 points per game. ===Houston Rockets=== On February 9, 2006, Bogans was traded to the Rockets for [[Lonny Baxter]]. [[Chuck Hayes]] and [[Gerald Fitch]], Bogans' former teammates at the University of Kentucky, along with himself, were all at one point members of the Rockets (although Fitch never actually played as he was released). ===Second stint with Orlando=== Bogans re-signed with the [[Orlando Magic|Magic]] in July 2006 as a free-agent.[http://www.nba.com/magic/news/Magic_Sign_Free_Agent_Keith_Bo-184494-800.html Magic Sign Free Agent Keith Bogans], [[Orlando Magic]] home page, July 13, 2006 On November 22, 2008, Bogans, starting his first game[https://web.archive.org/web/20081212010633/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=281122019 Yao has 22 points, 13 rebounds as Rockets snap Magic streak at five] of [[2008–09 NBA season|2008–09 season]], broke his thumb on his non-shooting hand in a game against the Houston Rockets.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3723181 Bogans, Magic's top reserve, to miss 4-6 weeks with broken thumb] He was expected to miss 4–6 weeks. However, he had the cast on his thumb removed on December 3{{Cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2008120319 |title=Howard leads Magic past Timberwolves 100-89 |access-date=July 21, 2014 |archive-date=January 5, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140105090710/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2008120319 |url-status=dead }} and [https://www.espn.com/nba/preview?gameId=281205019 Thunder-Magic Preview] returned two days later on December 5 against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], scoring 9 points in 26 minutes.[https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=281205019 Thunder 89, Magic 98 - Box score][http://www.hotboxsports.com/nba/player/1235 Hotbox Sports - Keith Bogans - Fantasy Basketball Profile] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100430021535/http://www.hotboxsports.com/nba/player/1235 |date=April 30, 2010 }} ===Milwaukee Bucks=== On February 5, 2009, Bogans was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], the team who initially drafted him, for guard [[Tyronn Lue]] and cash.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3886833 Magic acquire point guard Lue]{{cite news |url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/basketball/magic/orl-magic-trade-keith-bogans-for-tyronn-lue-story,0,5322161.story |title=Orlando Magic trade Keith Bogans for former Magic guard Tyronn Lue |last=Stephens |first=Tim |date=February 5, 2009 |publisher=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |access-date=February 5, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090207002304/http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/basketball/magic/orl-magic-trade-keith-bogans-for-tyronn-lue-story,0,5322161.story |archive-date=February 7, 2009 }} Bogans played only 29 games for the Bucks before leaving. In those 29 games Bogans averaged 6.0 points per game. ===San Antonio Spurs=== Bogans signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in September 2009.[http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/spurs/60116887.html Spurs obtain journeyman guard Bogans]{{dead link|date=January 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}. Retrieved on September 22, 2009. During the 2009–10 regular season with the Spurs, Bogans scored a season-high of 17 points against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] on April 13, 2010.[https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2010041224 Spurs rout T-Wolves, avoid 8th seed in West] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025211528/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2010041224 |date=October 25, 2012 }} on ''[[Yahoo!]] Sports''; Weber, Paul (April 13, 2010) Bogans only played one season with the Spurs. He played 79 games and started in 50 games. ===Chicago Bulls=== Bogans signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]] on August 11, 2010.[http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bogans_signs_100711.html Bulls sign guard Keith Bogans] During the 2010–11 regular season, Bogans was a starter for the Bulls, and averaged 4.4 points, 1.8 rebounds, and 1.2 assists in 82 games. Though his statistics were considered modest for a starter, coach [[Tom Thibodeau]] praised Bogans' defense, saying "If he's guarding you, you know he's guarding you. He's going to make you work. He's a physical player." Bogans said about his offense that people "need to understand that's not why I'm here. I'm on the floor with [[Luol Deng]], [[Derrick Rose]], [[Carlos Boozer]]... there aren't a lot of shots for me and [reserve center] [[Kurt Thomas (basketball)|Kurt Thomas]]."[https://www.chicagotribune.com/2011/01/30/bogans-scores-points-with-coaches-teammates/ Bogans scores points with coaches, teammates] on ''[[Chicago Tribune]]''; Johnson, K.C. (January 30, 2011) On March 15, 2011, Bogans scored a season-high 17 points in a win against the [[Washington Wizards]] to help the Bulls secure the top-seed of the Eastern Conference.[https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2011031504 Bulls win 7th straight, are alone atop East race] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110318232925/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2011031504 |date=March 18, 2011 }} on ''[[Yahoo! Sports]]'' (March 15, 2011) Bogans also scored 15 points in the fifth game of the first playoff series against the [[Indiana Pacers]] where the Bulls guaranteed their pass to the second round.[https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2011042604 Rose, Bulls eliminate Pacers, 116-89] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140813174517/https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2011042604 |date=August 13, 2014 }} on [[Yahoo!]] Sports (April 27, 2011) The Bulls made it to the [[NBA Conference Finals|Eastern Conference Finals]], where they lost to the [[Miami Heat]]. Bogans played and started in all postseason games.{{cite web|title=Heat stage late comeback to advance to NBA Finals, eliminate Bulls|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310526004|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110529001337/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310526004|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 29, 2011|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN}} On December 9, 2011, facing a $1.73 million option for 2011–12, the Bulls called Bogans off the court minutes before the first practice of the NBA season. The Bulls decided to hold out as long as they could regarding their decision on Bogans' contract, because they were waiting to see how the rest of the market for shooting guards was.[https://www.espn.com/chicago/nba/story/_/id/7335650/source-keith-bogans-pulled-first-chicago-bulls-practice Source: Bulls sit Keith Bogans] On December 16, 2011, Bogans was waived by the Bulls.[http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-waive-guard-keith-bogans.html Bulls Waive Guard Keith Bogans] ===New Jersey / Brooklyn Nets=== [[File:Keith Bogans against Bobcats.jpg|thumb|Bogans (left) defending [[Gerald Henderson Jr.|Gerald Henderson]], 2013]] On February 1, 2012, Bogans signed with the [[New Jersey Nets]].[https://www.espn.com/new-york/nba/story/_/id/7528220/new-jersey-nets-sign-ex-chicago-bulls-guard-keith-bogans-waive-larry-owens Nets sign guard Keith Bogans] Bogans was injured contesting a dunk by [[Detroit Pistons]] forward [[Greg Monroe]] on February 8, 2012, tearing a deltoid ligament. He was waived by the team on February 14, 2012, after playing five games.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/02/14/nets-emmett.ap/ |title=Injury-plagued Nets sign F Andre Emmett to 10-day contract |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=February 14, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140203024454/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/02/14/nets-emmett.ap/ |archive-date=February 3, 2014 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }} On July 19, 2012, he re-signed with the Nets for the 2012–13 season.{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10572 |title=Brooklyn Nets sign Keith Bogans |access-date=July 20, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140219002640/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10572 |archive-date=February 19, 2014 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }} Bogans played in 74 games in 2012–13, starting in 23 of them. He averaged 4.2 points per game. ===Boston Celtics=== On July 12, 2013, Bogans was [[sign and trade|signed and traded]] to the [[Boston Celtics]] as part of a blockbuster deal that sent Celtics stars [[Kevin Garnett]], [[Paul Pierce]], and [[Jason Terry]] to the Nets.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-complete-trade-brooklyn-nets|title=Celtics Complete Trade With Brooklyn Nets|work=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2013|access-date=July 13, 2013}} Bogans' final NBA game was played on January 7, 2014, in a 98 - 129 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]] where he recorded 9 points, 1 assist and 1 rebound. On January 14, 2014, he was excused from the team indefinitely for personal reasons.[https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4710091/bogans-excused-from-cs-indefinitely Bogans excused from C's indefinitely] ===Philadelphia 76ers=== On September 25, 2014, Bogans was traded, along with two future second-round picks, to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in exchange for [[John Lucas III]], [[Erik Murphy]], [[Dwight Powell]], [[Malcolm Thomas (basketball, born 1988)|Malcolm Thomas]] and the Cavaliers' 2016 and 2017 second-round picks.[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/boston-trade-140925 Cavs Complete Trade with Boston] On September 27, he was traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], along with a 2018 second-round pick, in exchange for a 2015 protected second-round pick.[http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/philadelphia-trade-140927 Cavs Complete Trade with Philadelphia] On October 7, 2014, he was waived by the 76ers before ever playing for the team.[http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141007-sixers-sign-two Sixers Sign Two Players] In July 2015, Bogans joined the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].[http://www.nba.com/blazers/overtime/following-year-bogans-just-happy-be-back-basketball Following Year Off, Bogans "Just Happy to be Back" in Basketball] At age 35, he was the oldest player
